subject: english
topic: Sentence interpretation: which option best explains the sentence

kept.q: Read the sentence carefully and choose the option that best explains it: 'By the time the invigilator entered the examination hall, only two candidates had completed the objective questions.'
options: The invigilator entered late, after most candidates had already left.
Exactly two candidates were absent from the examination.
Most candidates had not yet finished the objective questions when the invigilator came in.
The invigilator completed the objective questions for the candidates.
kept.explanation: 'By the time' shows that one event had already happened before another. Since only two candidates had finished, it means the rest were still working when the invigilator entered.
kept.pidgin: 'By the time' show say one thing don happen before another one. Na only two candidates don finish when invigilator enter, so the rest still dey work.

kept.q: Read the sentence carefully and choose the option that best explains it: 'The more carefully Aisha prepared her notes, the fewer mistakes she made in the test.'
options: Careful preparation of notes led to a reduction in Aisha's mistakes.
Aisha made many mistakes despite preparing her notes carefully.
The fewer mistakes Aisha made, the more carefully she prepared her notes.
Aisha's carefulness in preparing notes had no effect on her test performance.
kept.explanation: The 'the more... the fewer' structure shows a direct cause-and-effect link: as Aisha's care in preparing increased, her mistakes decreased.
kept.pidgin: 'The more... the fewer' structure dey show say as Aisha dey careful well well for her notes, na so her mistakes dey reduce.

kept.q: Read the sentence carefully and choose the option that best explains it: 'Unless the local government fixes the bad road, traders will keep losing goods to accidents.'
options: The local government has already fixed the road, so losses will stop.
Traders will lose goods only after the road has been fixed.
The bad road has nothing to do with the traders' losses.
The traders will stop losing goods only if the bad road is repaired.
kept.explanation: 'Unless' introduces the only condition that can stop the stated problem. Here, repairing the road is the only thing that will end the traders' losses.
kept.pidgin: 'Unless' na the only condition wey fit stop the problem. So na only if dem fix the road, traders go stop to dey lose their goods.

kept.q: Read the sentence carefully and choose the option that best explains it: 'Tunde's argument during the debate was like flogging a dead horse.'
options: Tunde presented a fresh and convincing new argument.
Tunde was wasting his effort on a point that no longer mattered.
Tunde refused to take part in the debate.
Tunde physically harmed an animal during the debate.
kept.explanation: 'Flogging a dead horse' is an idiom meaning to waste effort on something that is already settled or hopeless. It shows Tunde's point was pointless to keep pushing.
kept.pidgin: 'Flogging dead horse' na idiom wey mean say person dey waste time for something wey don already finish or no get hope. E show say Tunde point no dey useful again.

kept.q: Read the sentence carefully and choose the option that best explains it: 'Hardly any of the students failed to submit their assignment before the deadline.'
options: Almost none of the students submitted their assignment before the deadline.
No student submitted the assignment before the deadline.
Almost all the students submitted their assignment before the deadline.
Only a few students submitted their assignment before the deadline.
kept.explanation: This sentence has a double negative: 'hardly any' plus 'failed to'. The two negatives cancel each other out, so the real meaning is that almost all the students succeeded in submitting on time.
kept.pidgin: This sentence get double negative: 'hardly any' plus 'failed to'. The two negative dey cancel each other, so the real meaning be say almost everybody submit their work on time.

kept.q: Read the sentence carefully and choose the option that best explains it: 'Not a few of the candidates scored above average in the mock examination.'
options: A large number of candidates scored above average.
Only a handful of candidates scored above average.
No candidate scored above average.
Exactly one candidate scored above average.
kept.explanation: 'Not a few' is a figure of speech called litotes, which uses a negative to express a strong positive. It actually means 'many', so a large number of candidates scored above average.
kept.pidgin: 'Not a few' na litotes, na figure of speech wey use negative talk to show strong positive meaning. E mean 'plenty', so na plenty candidates score above average.
